query: measured cost of methods for For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and write both sides of that split onto the result the handling process reads. PalletPoseStamped gains the chosen candidate's source index as the pallet sent through stage 2, and the source indices of the other class-matched candidates in that same Detection2DArray as deferred. Those indices are the slots extract_detection_candidates already stored. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the roster is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, the same two lists go on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. Stage 2 still runs once. The user named which detections are sent versus deferred; the part they did not name is that both lists sit on PalletPoseStamped, the pose result for the AGV controller, rather than only on a diagnostic the success path does not use.
findings: Stage 2 still runs once, and that one call is the cost that scales if the other class-matched boxes enter it. CosyPose spent 190 ms of a 320 ms scene posing every candidate (4 views, 6 detections per view, one coarse iteration and one refine iteration); association was 40 ms and scene refinement 90 ms (Labbé et al., ECCV 2020). On pallet bins, RF-DETR-S detection was about 21 ms and FoundationPose about 2.8 s per frame on an i9-9920X and an RTX 2080 Ti, about 130 times the detector (Wu and Demeester, VISIGRAPP 2026). The deferred list is those other source indices, not a second pose.

A per-box chamfer is the same multiplier. Liu, Tuzel, Veeraraghavan, and Chellappa measured average detection at 0.71 s with directional chamfer, 29.1 s with chamfer matching, and 65.3 s with oriented chamfer (bin-picking, 2012). Classic chamfer was 17.59 µs per hypothesis on templates of about 1,610 points, and 1.05 million hypotheses took 0.42 s; directional chamfer was 0.40 µs per hypothesis (CVPR 2010). Once select_detection has named the box, stage 2 scores that crop once. Each deferred index is not another hypothesis search.

A whole-image second head does not get cheaper by deferring boxes. EfficientPose says detect-then-PnP runtime grows linearly with object count, while its single-shot φ=0 model stays nearly flat: 36.43 ms (27.45 FPS) for one object and 38.13 ms (26.22 FPS) on Occlusion images that typically hold eight (Bukschat and Vetter, 2020). T6D-Direct is 0.017 s and does not depend on instance count (58 fps, N=20 queries, RTX 3090). COPE's BOP time is 0.075 s, against CosyPose at 0.227 s and CDPNv2 at 1.010 s; at 15 instances it was about 7 times CosyPose and more than 12 times CDPNv2, with negligible growth up to 70 instances and real-time (>24 fps) through 90 (Thalhammer et al., WACV 2023). A pallet pose net was 5.49 ms inside a 27.5 ms pipeline (YOLOX 2.52 ms) on an RTX 4090 (Miura et al., VISAPP 2026). The saving here is skipping a per-box geometric stage, not shrinking a constant-time head.

Both index lists on PalletPoseStamped stay inside the flat part of the ROS 2 size curve. Kronauer et al. (SenSys 2021) measured equal end-to-end latency at 128 B, 1 KB, and 10 KB; it rose only at 100 KB and 500 KB, once UDP fragments past 64 KB. Fast DDS CDR, mean of three pinned-core runs, serializes a Pose in 14.9 ns, a Header in 14.3 ns, and a String in 10.7 ns (rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps pull 150). The chosen source index, the deferred source indices, and the RGB and depth stamps already on that message are a few integers and two builtin_interfaces/Time fields. The handling process that already reads this pose gets the roster in the same sample.

A diagnostic the success path does not use is the slow channel, not the cheap one. REP-107 publishes DiagnosticArray on /diagnostics at 1 Hz by default and says the channel is not a keepalive because aggregation can leave data stale. diagnostic_updater.period defaults to 1.0 s. diagnostic_aggregator pub_rate defaults to 1.0, and the aggregator publishes /diagnostics_agg at 1 Hz. A second topic is another hop: at a 128 B payload most of the time was DDS plus the rclcpp notification delay, and ROS 2 added up to 50% over raw DDS (Kronauer). Humble Fast-DDS 1:1 at a 4 KB buffer was 0.073 ms over UDP and 0.060 ms zero-copy (OSRF Sony report). Putting both lists on the pose the AGV controller already reads avoids that extra subscription and the 1 Hz period.

On estimate failure the same two lists ride the one diagnostic that path publishes. REP-107 stores hardware-specific data as string KeyValue pairs, so each index is two strings. At 10.7 ns per String that CDR is tens of nanoseconds, and the sample stays in the 128 B–10 KB band where latency did not change. The two early returns publish nothing, so they add no DDS sample and no second hop. The 1 Hz updater and aggregator rates apply when the failure result goes through that stock diagnostics path; a direct small publish is one hop at the 4 KB figure above, still the only result that path sends.

Writing the stored slots does not add a synchronization wait. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps. ApproximateTime with the default inter-message lower bound of 0 can delay a set by about one period T before it treats the match as optimal; a realistic lower bound lets the set publish when the later message arrives (ROS wiki). At 30 Hz that documented hold is about 33 ms, which dominates copying source indices extract_detection_candidates already stored.
